Total securities in bank credit were $5,781.4B, up $16.3B, seasonally adjusted. Banks added to their government-backed holdings in the week, with cash assets little changed at $3,213.5B, up $5.2B.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks, Oct. 23, 2026

items.headline: Fed calendar: no speeches or hearings listed Oct. 26-31; H.10 and CP data due Oct. 26
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's October calendar lists the two-day FOMC meeting on Oct. 27-28, with the press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 28, and no speeches, hearings or stress-test events for Oct. 26-31. Statistical releases include Commercial Paper at 1:00 p.m. and H.10 foreign exchange rates at 4:15 p.m. on Oct. 26, plus G.20 finance companies on Oct. 30 with an approximate publication date. The quiet speaker calendar leaves the FOMC statement and press conference as the main Fed communication of the week.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: Calendar, October 2026

items.headline: Fed minutes: most participants saw another rate increase likely appropriate by year end
items.take: The minutes of the Sept. 15-16 FOMC meeting, last updated Oct. 7, say most participants judged that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end. The Committee had voted 12-0 to raise the range by 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, and participants described inflation risk as skewed to the upside. With the next meeting on Oct. 27-28, the minutes frame the question as pace and timing of further tightening rather than whether it is on the table.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC minutes, Sept. 15-16, 2026

items.headline: Fed Sept. projections: median fed funds rate 4.1% for 2026, up from 3.8% in June
items.take: The Sept. 16 Summary of Economic Projections shows a median federal funds rate of 4.1% for 2026 (June: 3.8%), 4.1% for 2027 (3.6%) and 3.9% for 2028 (3.4%), with a longer-run median of 3.2% (3.1%). The current target range is 3-3/4 to 4 percent, so the 2026 median sits above the top of that range. The projections move the rate path higher in every year shown, which is the backdrop for the Oct. 27-28 meeting.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC projection materials, Sept. 16, 2026

items.headline: Fed Sept. projections: 2026 PCE inflation 3.7%, core 3.4%, unemployment 4.1%, GDP 2.3%
items.take: Median FOMC projections from Sept. 16 for 2026 are: PCE inflation 3.7% (June: 3.6%), core PCE inflation 3.4% (3.3%), unemployment rate 4.1% (4.3%) and real GDP growth 2.3% (2.2%). For 2027, PCE inflation is projected at 2.3% and core at 2.5%, unchanged from June. Officials marked inflation up and unemployment down for 2026, a combination that supports the case for firmer policy.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC projection materials, Sept. 16, 2026

items.headline: BLS: PPI final demand up 6.3% in 12 months to September, largest since December 2022
items.take: The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 6.3% over the 12 months ended September 2026, which BLS describes as the largest 12-month increase since 6.4% in December 2022. Final demand goods rose 9.8% and final demand services 4.9%; the data are not seasonally adjusted and subject to revision for four months. The goods-services gap shows how much of the pipeline pressure is concentrated in physical inputs.
items.source_name: BLS: The Economics Daily, Producer Price Index up 6.3 percent in September

items.headline: BLS PPI: gasoline up 64.3%, No. 2 diesel up 115.2% over 12 months to September
items.take: BLS reports final demand energy prices up 35.4% over the 12 months ended September, led by gasoline (+64.3%), No. 2 diesel (+115.2%) and home heating oil and distillates (+117.5%). Transportation and warehousing services rose 16.0%, including truck freight and water freight (both +19.3%) and airline passenger services (+16.6%). Fuel costs appear to be passing into freight and travel prices, which is how an energy shock reaches services.
items.source_name: BLS: The Economics Daily, Producer Price Index up 6.3 percent in September

items.headline: Fed minutes: interest on reserve balances raised to 3.90%, primary credit rate to 4.0%
items.take: The Sept. 15-16 FOMC minutes record that the interest rate on reserve balances was raised to 3.90 percent and the primary credit rate to 4.0 percent alongside the 1/4-point increase in the target range to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The minutes also say the Desk had paused reserve management purchases and that the pace of future purchases was not on a preset course. Both rates are administered by the Fed, so they will move only if the Committee changes policy on Oct. 28.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC minutes, Sept. 15-16, 2026

items.headline: Fed calendar: FOMC meets Oct. 27-28; press conference Oct. 28 at 2:30 p.m. ET
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's calendar lists a two-day FOMC meeting on Oct. 27-28, with the press conference on Oct. 28 at 2:30 p.m. ET. The calendar does not list a separate statement time. The meeting is the main scheduled U.S. policy event of the week, and it lands one day before the first estimate of third-quarter GDP.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: October 2026 calendar

items.headline: BEA schedules third-quarter GDP advance estimate and September income for Oct. 29
items.take: BEA's release schedule lists the advance estimate of third-quarter 2026 GDP and the September Personal Income and Outlays report for Oct. 29 at 8:30. Both arrive the day after the FOMC press conference, so the Fed's comments will come before the first read on the quarter. BEA also lists September international trade for Nov. 4.
items.source_name: BEA release schedule

items.headline: BLS Employment Cost Index for Q3 due Oct. 30 at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: BLS lists the Employment Cost Index for the third quarter of 2026 for Friday, Oct. 30 at 8:30 a.m. ET. It is the only BLS release on the schedule for the final day of the week. The ECI measures employer labor costs, which makes it one of the labor-cost gauges that sits alongside the BEA's income data the day before.
items.source_name: BLS release schedule, October 2026

items.headline: ECB Governing Council holds monetary policy meeting Oct. 28-29; press conference Oct. 29
items.take: The ECB's calendar lists the monetary policy meeting in Frankfurt on Oct. 28 and 29, with the press conference following on Oct. 29. The next meeting after that is Dec. 16-17, and the calendar does not list press conference times. The Oct. 29 decision day also coincides with BEA's third-quarter GDP release.
items.source_name: ECB Governing Council meeting calendar

items.headline: BLS: no releases Oct. 26-27; metro-area jobs and business dynamics data Oct. 28
items.take: BLS lists no releases for Oct. 26 or 27. On Wednesday, Oct. 28 at 10:00 a.m. ET it schedules Metropolitan Area Employment and Unemployment for September and Business Employment Dynamics for the first quarter of 2026. Consumer Expenditures for annual 2025 follows on Oct. 29 at 10:00 a.m. ET, so the early-week labor-data calendar is thin.
items.source_name: BLS release schedule, October 2026

items.headline: Fed statistical calendar: H.6 money stock Oct. 27; H.4.1 balance sheet Oct. 29
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's calendar lists H.6 (Money Stock Measures) on Oct. 27 at 1:00 p.m. and the H.4.1 balance sheet report on Oct. 29 at 4:30 p.m. H.8 bank assets and liabilities follows on Oct. 30 at 4:15 p.m., with H.15 rates published each day at 4:15 p.m. The H.4.1 will be the first weekly balance sheet look after the policy meeting.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: October 2026 calendar

items.headline: Treasury par curve: 10-year at 5.00% and 30-year at 5.33% on Oct. 23
items.take: Treasury's daily par yield curve for Oct. 23 showed the 2-year at 4.69%, 10-year at 5.00% and 30-year at 5.33%, each 4 basis points above Oct. 22. The 10-year was 15 basis points below its 5.15% on Oct. 19, and the 3-month bill at 4.22% sat 78 basis points under the 10-year.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury Daily Par Yield Curve Rates

items.headline: Treasury curve: 20-year yield 5.37% sits above 30-year at 5.33% on Oct. 23
items.take: Treasury's par yield curve showed the 20-year at 5.37% and the 30-year at 5.33% on Oct. 23, a 4 basis point inversion between the two longest maturities. The 7-year was 4.89% and the 10-year 5.00%, so the curve rises to the 20-year point and then dips slightly. The 20-year was 5.32% on Oct. 22.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury Daily Par Yield Curve Rates

items.headline: 10-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.34% on Oct. 23, up from 2.32%
items.take: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate, derived from nominal and inflation-indexed Treasury yields, was 2.34% on Oct. 23, 2026. It was 2.32% on Oct. 22, 2.37% on Oct. 21, and 2.35% on both Oct. 20 and Oct. 19. The range across the five observations is five basis points, suggesting market-implied inflation expectations were steady even as nominal yields moved.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board via FRED (T10YIE)

items.headline: 10-year TIPS real yield falls to 2.64% on Oct. 22 from 2.76% a day earlier
items.take: The 10-year inflation-indexed Treasury yield was 2.64% on Oct. 22, 2026, down 12 basis points from 2.76% on Oct. 21 and 16 basis points below 2.80% on Oct. 19. Nominal 10-year yields fell 17 basis points over the same two days (5.13% to 4.96%), so most of the decline came from real yields rather than breakevens.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board via FRED (DFII10)

items.headline: Fed overnight reverse repo take-up $0.2B on Oct. 23, little changed from earlier in week
items.take: Treasury securities sold in the Fed's overnight reverse repurchase operations totaled $0.200 billion on Oct. 23, 2026, versus $0.351 billion on Oct. 22, $0.237 billion on Oct. 21, $0.227 billion on Oct. 20 and $0.330 billion on Oct. 19. Usage has stayed under $0.4 billion all week, indicating minimal use of the facility.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board via FRED (RRPONTSYD)

items.headline: BioNTech, BMS report Phase 2 pumitamig data in second-line NSCLC at ESMO
items.take: In the single-arm Phase 2 ROSETTA Lung-107 study (abstract LBA76 at ESMO 2026), pumitamig 1400 mg plus docetaxel showed a confirmed objective response rate of 36.7% and disease control rate of 90.0% in 30 efficacy-evaluable patients. Median progression-free survival in 50 treated patients was 6.9 months; grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18.0%. BMS said it looks forward to defining the path forward for pumitamig in second-line NSCLC; overall survival was not reported.
items.source_name: BioNTech and Bristol Myers Squibb release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 25, 2026)

items.headline: Genmab reports petosemtamab Phase 2 colorectal data: ORR 75% first-line, 67% second-line
items.take: Genmab presented updated Phase 2 data at ESMO 2026 for petosemtamab plus FOLFOX or FOLFIRI in 79 treated patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (45 first-line, 34 second-line). Objective response rates (confirmed and unconfirmed) were 75% first-line and 67% second-line, with disease control rates of 95% and 93%. Median follow-up was 5.9 and 7.1 months, and Genmab will hold an investor update Oct. 28 at 12:00 p.m. EDT.
items.source_name: Genmab release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 25, 2026)

items.headline: Chicago Fed NFCI at -0.496 for week ended Oct. 16, looser than average
items.take: The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index read -0.496 for the week ending October 16, 2026, up from -0.502 the prior week and -0.508 on October 2. Per the series notes, positive values indicate financial conditions tighter than average, so a negative reading means looser than average. Conditions have stayed loose while edging up for three straight weeks; the next reading is due October 28.
items.source_name: Chicago Fed via FRED (NFCI)

items.headline: Chicago Fed adjusted NFCI at -0.518 for week ended Oct. 16
items.take: The Chicago Fed's Adjusted National Financial Conditions Index, which isolates financial conditions uncorrelated with economic conditions, was -0.518 for the week ending October 16, 2026, versus -0.524 the prior week. Negative values indicate conditions looser than average. Both the adjusted and unadjusted gauges rose by 0.006 on the week, computed from the published readings.
items.source_name: Chicago Fed via FRED (ANFCI)

items.headline: Fed note: semiliquid retail funds grew from $15B in 2018 to $388B in 2025
items.take: A Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note by Logan George and Chaehee Shin finds total net assets of interval funds, tender offer funds and non-traded perpetual-life BDCs rose from $15 billion in 2018 to $388 billion in 2025, while total mutual fund net assets grew 33% over the same period. The interval and tender offer figures are lower-bound estimates, and non-traded BDC assets were about $307 billion at 2025Q4. The growth rate of roughly 26 times in seven years makes these vehicles a fast-growing channel for retail exposure to private credit.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, FEDS Notes (Oct. 14)

items.headline: Fed note: interval funds hold 49.5% private credit; non-traded BDC debt-to-equity 0.90
items.take: In the Fed Board's 2025Q4 sample of 207 funds, interval funds held 49.5% of value-weighted assets in private credit, tender offer funds 13.4%, and non-traded BDCs 93.4% in loans. Average debt-to-equity was 0.27 for interval funds, 0.09 for tender offer funds and 0.90 for non-traded BDCs, and average default or non-accrual rates were 0.6%, 2.4% and 1.4%. The note cites defined contribution plans holding over $13.9 trillion as of September 2025, which frames why retail access to these funds draws regulatory attention.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, FEDS Notes (Oct. 14)

items.headline: CFTC: 10-year note futures show asset managers net long 2.93M, leveraged funds net short 2.11M
items.take: CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report for October 20, 2026 shows UST 10Y note open interest of 5,868,295 contracts, with asset managers long 3,675,600 and short 750,184 (net long 2,925,416) and leveraged funds long 567,553 and short 2,674,777 (net short 2,107,224). Those net figures are computed from the report's long and short columns. Asset managers and leveraged funds sit on opposite sides of the 10-year contract, with asset managers' net long equal to about 50% of open interest.
items.source_name: CFTC, Traders in Financial Futures (Oct. 20 data)

items.headline: CFTC: 2-year note futures asset managers net long 1.72M vs leveraged funds net short 1.29M
items.take: In CFTC's October 20, 2026 financial futures report, UST 2Y note open interest was 4,533,571 contracts: asset managers were long 2,461,884 and short 738,304 (net long 1,723,580), while leveraged funds were long 771,136 and short 2,056,684 (net short 1,285,548). For Ultra UST Bond, open interest was 2,364,949, asset managers net long 849,383 and leveraged funds net short 804,808. Net figures are computed from the report's columns, so the same asset-manager-long, leveraged-fund-short split shows up in all three contracts.
items.source_name: CFTC, Traders in Financial Futures (Oct. 20 data)

items.headline: NY Fed: each 1-pt rise in average tariffs lifts consumer goods prices about 0.25%
items.take: New York Fed staff (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein) estimate that each one-percentage-point rise in average tariffs raises consumer goods prices by about 0.25% after one year, with roughly two-thirds coming through imported consumer goods. They find about 90% of the 2025 tariffs passed through to U.S. import prices, and project the tariff contribution to 12-month inflation reaching roughly zero by August 2026 before turning negative. The authors' result frames tariffs as a price-level effect that drops out of year-over-year comparisons, which matters for how goods inflation is read.
items.source_name: New York Fed, Liberty Street Economics (Oct. 6)

items.headline: NY Fed study: most firms' investment responds little to monetary policy
items.take: A New York Fed Liberty Street post (Oct. 7) finds investment by most firms in most periods responds little to monetary policy, though investment falls when rates rise for all firms. For about 5% of firm-quarters, a monetary shock raising the fed funds rate 1 percentage point lowers capital growth by 4 percentage points, and small and young firms respond most. The takeaway is that rate transmission runs through a minority of firms at any given time, with the sample limited to publicly listed Compustat firms.
items.source_name: New York Fed, Liberty Street Economics (Oct. 7)

items.headline: BOJ's Koeda: neutral rate 'considerably above 1 percent' ahead of Oct. 29-30 meeting
items.take: In an Oct. 15 speech, BOJ Policy Board member Junko Koeda said the September hike raised the overnight call rate to around 1.25%, that the neutral interest rate is "considerably above 1 percent," and that the Bank "should not become overly cautious about raising the policy interest rate." She also said the median of item-level inflation is in the early 2% range. Her remarks are one board member's view and set the tone going into the Oct. 29-30 meeting, which carries an Outlook Report.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan (speech by Junko Koeda, Oct. 15)

items.headline: BOJ Sept. meeting opinions: several backed a hike, others favored holding
items.take: The BOJ's Summary of Opinions for the Sept. 17-18 meeting, released Oct. 1, shows several members supported raising the policy rate while others preferred holding because CPI had been below 2%. Members described underlying inflation as "fairly close to 2 percent" and said further hikes should be gradual and flexible, with the pace faster if upward price deviation appears. The split on timing is the backdrop for the Oct. 29-30 meeting.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan, Summary of Opinions (Sept. 17-18 meeting)

items.headline: Treasury tentative schedule: 2-, 5-, 7-year notes and 2-year FRN auction Oct. 26-29
items.take: Treasury's tentative auction schedule lists a 2-year note on Oct. 26, a 5-year note on Oct. 27, a 2-year FRN on Oct. 28 and a 7-year note on Oct. 29, all settling Nov. 2. Bill auctions run alongside, including 13- and 26-week bills on Oct. 26 and a 52-week bill on Oct. 27. The schedule gives no offering amounts yet, so size and demand are the things to watch once the announcements post.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury Tentative Auction Schedule

items.headline: Bank of Canada to announce rate decision Oct. 28 at 9:45 a.m. ET with Monetary Policy Report
items.take: The Bank of Canada will announce its overnight rate target decision on Oct. 28 at 9:45 a.m. ET, together with the Monetary Policy Report; Governor Macklem and Senior Deputy Governor Rogers hold a press conference at about 10:30 a.m. ET. The Bank's Sept. 2 release set the overnight rate target at 2.25%, with a Bank Rate of 2.5% and deposit rate of 2.20%. The decision lands the same day as the FOMC statement.
items.source_name: Bank of Canada

items.headline: Bank of Japan meets Oct. 29-30; Outlook Report due Oct. 30
items.take: The Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy Meeting is scheduled for Oct. 29 and 30, with the Outlook Report released Oct. 30. The Summary of Opinions follows on Nov. 10 at 8:50 a.m. and the minutes on Dec. 23. The BOJ meeting closes out a run of major central bank decisions that includes the FOMC and ECB earlier in the same week.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meetings

items.headline: Eurostat calendar lists euro-area Q3 preliminary GDP flash for Oct. 30
items.take: Eurostat's quarterly national accounts calendar lists the preliminary Q3 2026 GDP flash release for Friday, Oct. 30, with the fuller employment and GDP flash on Nov. 13. Eurostat marks these dates as provisional until confirmed in its weekly release calendar. The Oct. 30 print arrives the day after the ECB's Oct. 29 press conference.
items.source_name: Eurostat QNA release calendar

items.headline: Fed G.17: September industrial production up 0.7%, 2.2% above a year earlier
items.take: The Federal Reserve's G.17 release says industrial production rose 0.7 percent in September after edging up 0.1 percent in August, with August revised up from 0.0 percent. Total output stood at 104.0 percent of its 2017 average and was 2.2 percent above its year-earlier level. Utilities output rose 3.5 percent in the month, so the headline gain leaned on weather-sensitive output more than on factories.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed G.17: capacity utilization 76.9% in September; manufacturing output up 0.3%
items.take: Capacity utilization moved up to 76.9 percent in September, the Fed reported, with August revised up from 76.3 percent to 76.4 percent. Manufacturing output rose 0.3 percent in September, and August was revised from -0.3 percent to -0.2 percent. Mining output rose 0.2 percent; the factory gain was far smaller than the 0.7 percent increase in the overall index.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed adds private credit to Financial Accounts from September 2026 release
items.take: A Fed Board FEDS Note dated Oct. 16 says private credit assets under management reached over $2.6 trillion as of 2025:Q4, up from about $350 billion in 2012, and that integration into the Financial Accounts (Z.1) begins with the September 2026 release. Private credit was about 6 percent of total nonfinancial business debt in 2025:Q4 ($1.31 trillion of $23.29 trillion). The authors say the change does not substantially change business-debt trends overall, but it gives policymakers a first official sector-level view of a market that was previously recorded mostly as miscellaneous liabilities.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note: Introducing Private Credit into the Financial Accounts of the United States (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed note sizes private credit: private debt funds $939B, BDCs $572B in assets
items.take: The Fed's FEDS Note puts 2025:Q4 assets at about $939 billion for private debt funds, with private credit loans about 60 percent of that, and about $572 billion for business development companies, about 80 percent in private credit loans. Interval and tender offer funds held about $292 billion, up from $100 billion in 2021, and middle-market CLOs held $54 billion of private credit loans. The fast growth of the interval-fund channel is the part of the estimate worth watching.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note: Introducing Private Credit into the Financial Accounts of the United States (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed note: stock-bond correlation turned negative after 2021, weakening bond hedge
items.take: A Fed FEDS Note (Oct. 16) finds the correlation of U.S. stock returns with changes in 10-year yields was 0.4 in 2000-2021 and -0.09 after 2021; the euro-area figures were 0.41 and -0.02 and the U.K.'s 0.31 and -0.14. The U.S. 10-year yield's response to inflation news rose from a coefficient of 0.048 (2000-2019) to 0.155 post-2021. The authors attribute the shift to inflation dynamics and the mix of shocks, not to a change in bonds themselves, and say the hedge could improve if inflation eases.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note: Government Bonds' Safe-Haven Property and Inflationary Pressures (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Glacier Bancorp Q3 net income $104.6M; diluted EPS $0.80 vs. $0.57
items.take: Glacier Bancorp reported third-quarter net income of $104.562 million and diluted EPS of $0.80, versus $0.57 in Q3 2025 and $0.75 in Q2 2026. Net income was $67.9 million a year earlier, and total income was $329.8 million versus $260.7 million. The Guaranty Bancshares acquisition, with $3.357 billion of assets, closed Oct. 1, 2025, after the prior-year quarter ended, so the comparison spans a larger balance sheet.
items.source_name: Glacier Bancorp Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Glacier Bancorp NIM 4.01%; assets $32.29B, deposits $25.27B, loans $21.62B
items.take: Glacier reported a tax-equivalent net interest margin of 4.01% for Q3 2026, with total assets of $32.291 billion, deposits of $25.273 billion and loans receivable of $21.620 billion at Sept. 30. The board declared a $0.35 quarterly dividend on Sept. 22, payable Oct. 15 to holders of record Oct. 6. Deposits equal about 78% of assets, a funding base worth comparing with regional peers reporting this week.
items.source_name: Glacier Bancorp Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Heritage Financial Q3 net income $18.7M, EPS $0.46; board OKs 5% buyback
items.take: Heritage Financial reported Q3 2026 net income of $18.72 million and diluted EPS of $0.46, versus $0.55 in Q3 2025; net income was $17.5 million in Q2 2026 and $19.2 million a year earlier. On Oct. 21 the board approved a program to repurchase up to 5% of outstanding shares, about 2.0 million shares, replacing a prior program that was substantially completed in Q3. The company bought 341,483 shares for about $10.2 million in the quarter, so per-share earnings fell on the year while capital return continued.
items.source_name: Heritage Financial Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Heritage Financial NIM 4.05%; assets $8.52B, deposits $7.19B at Sept. 30
items.take: Heritage Financial reported a Q3 2026 net interest margin of 4.05%, total assets of $8,517.9 million and total deposits of $7,186.9 million at Sept. 30. It declared a $0.25 per-share dividend on Oct. 21, payable Nov. 18 to holders of record Nov. 4. Deposits equal about 84% of assets.
items.source_name: Heritage Financial Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Byline Bancorp Q3 net income $41.8M; diluted EPS $0.94 vs. $0.82
items.take: Byline Bancorp reported Q3 2026 net income of $41.786 million and diluted EPS of $0.94, versus $0.82 in Q3 2025, a 14.6% increase. Its net interest margin was 4.33% for the quarter. A margin above 4.3% is the figure to weigh against the 4.0%-4.1% margins other regional lenders reported this week.
items.source_name: Byline Bancorp Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Byline Bancorp total assets $9.90B, deposits $8.04B; dividend $0.14
items.take: Byline reported total assets of $9,898.8 million and total deposits of $8,039.1 million at Sept. 30, 2026, and declared a $0.14 per-share common dividend on Oct. 6. Deposits equal about 81% of assets.
items.source_name: Byline Bancorp Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Midland States Q3 diluted EPS $0.95 vs. $0.24; net interest margin 4.03%
items.take: Midland States Bancorp reported Q3 2026 net income available to common shareholders of $20.6 million ($22.8 million before preferred dividends) and diluted EPS of $0.95, versus $0.24 in Q3 2025. Net interest margin was 4.03%, with total assets of $6.82 billion and deposits of $5.62 billion at Sept. 30. The prior-year base was low, so the year-over-year gain is large in percentage terms.
items.source_name: Midland States Bancorp Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: First American Q3 net income $177.0M, diluted EPS $1.72 vs $1.84 a year earlier
items.take: First American Financial reported third-quarter 2026 total revenues of $2,084.6M, versus $1,978.9M a year earlier, and net income of $177.0M versus $189.6M. Net income per diluted share was $1.72 versus $1.84, while adjusted EPS was $1.78 versus $1.70. Revenue rose 5.3% on the year while GAAP diluted EPS fell 6.5%, so the quarter shows higher revenue paired with lower reported profit.
items.source_name: First American Financial Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1, Oct. 21, 2026)

items.headline: First American title pretax margin 12.4% vs 12.9%; home warranty 9.9% vs 14.1%
items.take: In Q3 2026, First American's Title Insurance and Services segment reported total revenues of $1,972.9M, versus $1,835.9M a year earlier. Its pretax margin was 12.4% versus 12.9%, with an adjusted pretax margin of 12.7% versus 12.9%; the Home Warranty pretax margin was 9.9% versus 14.1%. Segment revenue grew about 7.5% while margins narrowed, so title-segment profit did not keep pace with sales.

items.headline: Southern Realty Trust, Sunrise Realty Trust stockholders approve merger; close expected Nov. 5
items.take: Stockholders of Southern Realty Trust and Sunrise Realty Trust approved their merger on Oct. 23, with closing expected Nov. 5, 2026, subject to remaining customary conditions. Each SRT share converts into 1.45 newly issued SUNS shares plus $0.05 in cash, and former SRT holders are expected to own about 39% of the combined company. The 1.45 ratio reflects a 6.0% premium to SRT's book value per share relative to SUNS, a book-value-based exchange rather than a market-price one.
items.source_name: Southern Realty Trust press release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: UK September public borrowing £24.5B, up £1.8B on year; FYTD £97.8B: ONS
items.take: ONS puts UK public sector net borrowing (excluding banks) at £24.5 billion in September 2026, up £1.8 billion from £22.8 billion a year earlier and £1.9 billion above the OBR forecast. Borrowing for the financial year to September is £97.8 billion, down £4.4 billion on the year but £6.0 billion above forecast, or 3.1% of GDP. Borrowing is lower than a year ago for the year to date yet above the OBR's forecast, so the comparison depends on which benchmark is used.
items.source_name: ONS Public sector finances, UK: September 2026 (released Oct. 21, 2026)

items.headline: UK debt interest £10.9B in September, highest for the month since 1997: ONS
items.take: ONS reports central government debt interest payable of £10.9 billion in September 2026, up £1.6 billion (16.6%) on a year earlier and £2.0 billion above forecast, the highest September figure since monthly records began in 1997. ONS attributes £4.0 billion of the month's total to the capital uplift on index-linked gilts, which tracks RPI inflation. Because the uplift is tied to RPI inflation, index-linked gilts link inflation readings directly to monthly debt interest.
items.source_name: ONS Public sector finances, UK: September 2026 (released Oct. 21, 2026)

items.headline: UK public sector net debt provisionally £3,005.0B, above £3 trillion for first time: ONS
items.take: ONS provisionally estimates public sector net debt at £3,005.0 billion at end-September 2026, up £91.7 billion on a year earlier and, per the bulletin, above £3 trillion for the first time. As a share of GDP it is 94.0%, 0.7 percentage points lower than a year earlier and 1.2 points below the OBR forecast. Debt is rising in pounds while shrinking relative to the economy, so the GDP ratio is the number that frames the fiscal debate.
items.source_name: ONS Public sector finances, UK: September 2026 (released Oct. 21, 2026)

items.headline: Census week ahead: durable goods and new home sales both due Oct. 27
items.take: The Census Bureau's economic indicators calendar lists the Advance Report on Durable Goods for September at 8:30 a.m. and New Residential Sales for September at 10:00 a.m. on Oct. 27. The prior new home sales release put August at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 684,000, up 6.4% from July's 643,000, with 8.5 months' supply at the current sales rate. That August change was not statistically significant, so the September print is the first test of whether the rebound holds.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau economic indicators calendar; New Residential Sales, August 2026

items.headline: Census calendar: advance indicators Oct. 28; trade, factory orders and construction follow

Construction Spending for September follows Nov. 2 at 10:00 a.m., the full factory orders report Nov. 3 at 10:00 a.m., and U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services Nov. 4 at 8:30 a.m. These releases arrive alongside the Oct. 29 BEA GDP and personal income reports, so a cluster of Q3 data lands within about a week.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau economic indicators calendar

items.take: The Fed's H.4.1 shows reserve balances with Federal Reserve Banks averaging $2,962.6 billion in the week ended Oct. 21, down $59.5 billion from the prior week and up $29.6 billion from a year earlier. The Wednesday Oct. 21 level was $2,969.5 billion. Treasury General Account averaged $952.0 billion, up $68.6 billion on the week, so Treasury cash building is the line that moves against reserves in the same release.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.4.1 (release of Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Fed holds $4,571.2B Treasuries and $1,897.3B MBS in week to Oct. 21: H.4.1
items.take: H.4.1 shows U.S. Treasury securities held outright averaging $4,571.2 billion in the week ended Oct. 21, up $1.3 billion on the week and $374.8 billion from a year earlier. Mortgage-backed securities averaged $1,897.3 billion, down $0.8 billion on the week and $187.3 billion on the year. The year-over-year changes show the portfolio's composition shifting toward Treasuries and away from MBS.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.4.1 (release of Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: RBA cash rate target at 4.60% after unanimous 25 bp hike; next decision Nov. 3
items.take: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board raised the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.60% on Sept. 29, and its statement said the decision was unanimous. The Board said the three increases in the cash rate target since the beginning of the year have tightened financial conditions and the economy appears to be slowing. The RBA lists its next scheduled update for Nov. 3 at 2:30 p.m. Sydney time, the next test of whether the Board keeps tightening or pauses.
items.source_name: Reserve Bank of Australia, Monetary Policy Decision (Sept. 29, 2026)

items.headline: 3-month Treasury yield 34 bp above effective fed funds rate on Oct. 22: Fed H.15
items.take: The Fed's H.15 shows the 3-month Treasury constant-maturity yield at 4.22% on Oct. 22 against an effective federal funds rate of 3.88%, a gap of 34 basis points. On Oct. 21 the yield was 4.25%, a 37 bp gap. A bill yield that sits above the policy-rate benchmark is one way to read the short end of the curve as pricing less easing than a cut-friendly path would imply.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.15 Selected Interest Rates (release of Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: 2s10s Treasury spread at 31 bp on Oct. 22 as 2-year yield falls to 4.65%: Fed H.15
items.take: H.15 data show the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.65% on Oct. 22, down from 4.81% a day earlier, while the 10-year fell to 4.96% from 5.13%. The 10-year minus 2-year spread was 31 bp, against 32 bp on Oct. 21. The front end fell 16 bp and the 10-year 17 bp, so the curve shifted lower in near-parallel fashion rather than steepening or flattening.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.15 Selected Interest Rates (release of Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: AA nonfinancial commercial paper yields 3.95% at 30 days on Oct. 22: Fed

items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board Commercial Paper Rates and Outstanding (data as of Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: U.S. regular gasoline $4.284 a gallon on Oct. 19, down 4.7 cents on the week: EIA

items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update

items.headline: California regular gasoline $6.031 on Oct. 19; Gulf Coast lowest at $3.784: EIA

items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update

items.headline: Packaging Corp guides Q4 EPS ex-special items to $2.81; three mills face maintenance outages

Higher outage expenses and rising freight, fiber, chemical and energy costs frame the step down.

items.headline: BOJ Financial System Report: Japan's system 'stable on the whole'; banks pass oil, AI, rate stress
items.take: The Bank of Japan's October 2026 Financial System Report, released Oct. 23, says Japan's financial system "has been maintaining stability on the whole," with firms' loan demand rising and banks lending actively. It finds Japanese banks have enough capital and stable funding to withstand a global-financial-crisis-level stress and a compound shock of higher oil prices, an AI-expectations decline and sharply higher interest rates, and flags the Middle East, AI-related investment profitability and foreign non-bank intermediaries for close monitoring. The stress-test framing shows the central bank is probing energy and AI-valuation channels alongside traditional credit risk.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan, Financial System Report (October 2026)

items.headline: Treasury proposes rule limiting large investors' single-family home buying from 2027
items.take: Treasury on Oct. 22 issued proposed regulations implementing Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Starting January 7, 2027, large institutional investors would generally be barred from buying single-family homes unless the purchase is an excepted purchase, such as build-to-rent, renovate-to-rent or a homeownership program; the statute defines a large investor partly as one with investment control over at least 350 single-family homes. Public comments are due within 30 days after Federal Register publication, so the final exceptions will determine how much institutional buying the rule actually reaches.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury press release (Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury proposes outbound investment rule for AI, chips, quantum, hypersonics, biotech
items.take: Treasury on Oct. 22 issued a proposed rule to update the Outbound Investment Security Program under the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act. It would require U.S. persons to notify Treasury of certain transactions with covered foreign persons engaged in notifiable technologies and bar certain other transactions tied to prohibited technologies, across semiconductors and microelectronics, AI, quantum information technologies, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and hypersonic systems; the Secretary also added biotechnology. Final regulations will set an effective date, so U.S. investors with cross-border exposure to these sectors have a compliance rule to track.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury press release (Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Boeing to release Q3 results Oct. 27; call at 10:30 a.m. ET
items.take: Boeing said it will release third-quarter 2026 results on Tuesday, Oct. 27, with a conference call at 10:30 a.m. ET led by CEO Kelly Ortberg and CFO Jay Malave. The webcast, news release and presentation materials will be posted on Boeing's investor site. The company did not give a release time on its announcement page.
items.source_name: Boeing investor relations (announced Sept. 30, 2026)

items.headline: O'Reilly to report Q3 results after 3:30 p.m. CT Oct. 28; call Oct. 29
items.take: O'Reilly Automotive said its third-quarter 2026 results will be released after 3:30 p.m. Central Time on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. The conference call is Thursday, Oct. 29, at 10:00 a.m. Central Time, with a webcast on the company's investor relations site. A replay will be available through Oct. 28, 2027.
items.source_name: O'Reilly Automotive 8-K Ex. 99.1 (Oct. 1, 2026)

items.headline: CRH completes acquisition of Arcosa; total enterprise value about $8.5B
items.take: CRH said Oct. 23 that it has completed its acquisition of Arcosa, Inc., described as a leading U.S. provider of aggregates and critical infrastructure products, at a total enterprise value of approximately $8.5 billion under the June 22, 2026 agreement. CRH said it will issue updated full-year 2026 guidance reflecting the acquisition with its third-quarter results on Oct. 29. That release is the first place to look for how the deal changes CRH's reported figures.
items.source_name: CRH press release (Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: FHLB Des Moines Q3 net income $200M vs. $259M; advances $136.1B
items.take: The Federal Home Loan Bank of Des Moines reported preliminary Q3 2026 net income of $200 million versus $259 million in Q3 2025, with net interest income of $314 million versus $335 million. Advances were $136,089 million at Sept. 30, up $25.9 billion from $110,230 million at Dec. 31, 2025, and total assets were $217,362 million. Balance sheet growth alongside lower quarterly income is the pattern to note, and other expense rose to $103 million from $59 million.
items.source_name: Federal Home Loan Bank of Des Moines Q3 2026 release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: FHLB Des Moines dividend 9.95% on activity stock; $194M payable Nov. 10
items.take: FHLB Des Moines declared annualized dividend rates of 9.95% on average activity-based stock and 6.95% on average membership stock, unchanged from the prior quarter, with total payments of $194 million expected Nov. 10, 2026. Retained earnings were $3,985 million versus $3,797 million at year-end 2025, and the regulatory capital ratio was 5.45% versus 5.54%. Dividends are paid to member institutions that hold the bank's stock, so the rate reflects the bank's earnings returned to members.
items.source_name: Federal Home Loan Bank of Des Moines Q3 2026 release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: BEA to release Q3 advance GDP and September income and outlays Oct. 29
items.take: The Bureau of Economic Analysis schedule lists "GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026" and "Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026" for Oct. 29 at 8:30 a.m. ET. U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services for September follows on Nov. 4 at 8:30 a.m. Both Oct. 29 releases land the morning after the FOMC's Oct. 28 decision and on the same day as the ECB's.
items.source_name: BEA release schedule

items.headline: ECB Governing Council meets Oct. 28-29; press conference Oct. 29
items.take: The ECB's calendar shows its October monetary policy meeting on Oct. 28 and 29, with a press conference on Oct. 29. The next meeting is Dec. 16-17, with a press conference on Dec. 17. The Oct. 29 decision shares a day with U.S. advance Q3 GDP, so U.S. and euro-area signals arrive together.
items.source_name: ECB: Meetings of the Governing Council

items.headline: Gentex Q3 sales $647.7M vs. $655.2M; diluted EPS $0.43 vs. $0.46
items.take: Gentex reported Q3 2026 net sales of $647.7 million versus $655.2 million a year earlier, with GAAP net income of $90.6 million versus $101.0 million and diluted EPS of $0.43 versus $0.46. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.47 in both periods, and gross margin was 33.4% versus 34.4%, which the company attributed mainly to higher precious metal costs and lower-than-expected sales. Sales slipped 1.1% while GAAP EPS fell 6.5%, so the gap between GAAP and flat adjusted EPS is the detail to read in the release.
items.source_name: Gentex Q3 2026 earnings release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: Gentex narrows 2026 revenue view to ~$2.65B; gross margin 34.0%-34.5%
items.take: Gentex now expects 2026 consolidated revenue of approximately $2.65 billion, versus a prior $2.65-$2.75 billion range, and gross margin of 34.0%-34.5%, versus 34.5%-35.5% before. Its 2027 revenue outlook of $2.80-$2.90 billion is maintained and assumes primary-market light vehicle production declines about 1%. The prior range's upper half has been removed while 2027 is held, so the 2027 outlook is held while the 2026 range is trimmed.
items.source_name: Gentex Q3 2026 earnings release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: Gentex bought 5.7M shares for $132.6M in Q3; dividend held at $0.12
items.take: Gentex repurchased 5.7 million shares for $132.6 million in Q3 2026, at an average of $23.44 per share, and 11.6 million shares for $270.2 million year to date. The quarterly dividend declared was $0.12 per share, unchanged from Q3 2025. Q3 buybacks were nearly half of the nine-month total, which is a notable weighting in a quarter when net income fell.
items.source_name: Gentex Q3 2026 earnings release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: Preferred Bank Q3 diluted EPS $2.73 vs. $2.84; deposits $6.55B
items.take: Preferred Bank reported Q3 2026 net income of $32.9 million, down $3.0 million from $35.9 million in Q3 2025 and down from $33.5 million in Q2, with diluted EPS of $2.73 versus $2.84 a year earlier. Total deposits were $6.55 billion, up $77.7 million from June 30, and total assets were $7.82 billion. The quarterly dividend was $0.80 per share, up from $0.75 a year earlier, so payouts rose while per-share earnings fell.
items.source_name: Preferred Bank Q3 2026 earnings release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: ExxonMobil to release Q3 2026 results Friday, Oct. 30, at 5:30 a.m. CT
items.take: ExxonMobil said it will release third-quarter 2026 financial results on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, with the press release at 5:30 a.m. CT and a live conference call at 8:30 a.m. CT. The date is one week from today and gives energy readers a fixed point to compare with SLB's Oct. 23 results.
items.source_name: ExxonMobil investor relations announcement

items.headline: Bank of England Bank Rate stands at 3.75%; next MPC announcement Nov. 5
items.take: The Bank of England's website lists the current Bank Rate at 3.75%, published Sept. 17, 2026, with the next announcement due Nov. 5, 2026. The page does not state the Committee's vote split. Norges Bank's next decision is on the same day, Nov. 5, 2026.
items.source_name: Bank of England: Interest rates and Bank Rate

items.headline: Norges Bank policy rate 4.5%; next decision Nov. 5
items.take: Norges Bank lists its policy rate at 4.5%, published Sept. 24, 2026, and says the next policy rate decision will be announced on Nov. 5, 2026. The Bank of England's next decision is on the same day. Two European central banks with a Nov. 5 announcement make that date a shared checkpoint for global rates.
items.source_name: Norges Bank: Policy rate

items.headline: SLB Q3 revenue $9.45B, up 6%; diluted EPS $0.49 vs. $0.50
items.take: SLB reported Q3 2026 revenue of $9,449 million versus $8,928 million a year earlier and $8,972 million in Q2. GAAP net income attributable to SLB was $735 million versus $739 million, and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.49 versus $0.50; EPS excluding charges and credits was $0.64 versus $0.69. Revenue grew while per-share earnings slipped, so the mix of segments below is where the story sits.
items.source_name: SLB Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99)

items.headline: SLB North America revenue $2.40B, up 24%; Production Systems $4.00B
items.take: SLB's North America revenue was $2,401 million versus $1,930 million a year earlier, while International was $6,993 million versus $6,916 million. Production Systems revenue was $4,000 million versus $3,474 million; Reservoir Performance and Well Construction each fell 3%, to $1,634 million and $2,888 million. The release says the ChampionX businesses, acquired in July 2025, contributed $956 million of North America revenue in Q3 2026, so the 24% figure is not like-for-like.
items.source_name: SLB Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99)

items.headline: SLB repurchased 12.9M shares for $656M in Q3; quarterly dividend $0.295
items.take: SLB generated $1.51 billion of cash flow from operations and $828 million of free cash flow in Q3 2026, and repurchased 12.9 million shares for $656 million. The board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.295 per share, payable Jan. 7, 2027 to holders of record Dec. 2. Full-year 2026 capital investment is still expected to be about $2.5 billion.
items.source_name: SLB Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99)

items.headline: Treasury's cash at the Fed $945.2B on Oct. 21, up $59.3B on the week
items.take: The Fed's H.4.1 for the week ended Oct. 21 shows the Treasury General Account at $945,153 million on Wednesday, up $59,330 million from a week earlier. Reserve balances were $2,969,522 million and reverse repurchase agreements $334,083 million; total Fed assets were $6,753,604 million, down $2,035 million. A larger Treasury balance drains reserves from the banking system, which is why the TGA is watched alongside funding markets.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.4.1 (released Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury 2-year yield 4.81% on Oct. 21; 10-year 5.13%, 30-year 5.42%
items.take: The Fed's H.15 shows the 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 4.81% on Oct. 21, up from 4.77% on Oct. 19, while the 10-year was 5.13% and the 30-year 5.42%. The 3-month yield was 4.25% against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88%. That leaves the 2s10s spread at 32 basis points, with the FOMC meeting Oct. 27-28.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: American Express Q3 revenue $20.06B; diluted EPS $5.42 vs. $4.14
items.take: American Express reported Q3 2026 revenues net of interest expense of $20,062 million versus $18,426 million a year earlier, up 9%. Net income was $3,712 million versus $2,902 million, and diluted EPS was $5.42 versus $4.14; adjusted EPS was $4.68, up 13%. The gap between GAAP and adjusted EPS is the line to read closely in the release's reconciliation.
items.source_name: American Express Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: AmEx raises 2026 EPS guidance to $18.30-$18.60; $17.60-$17.90 adjusted
items.take: American Express said it is raising full-year EPS guidance to between $18.30 and $18.60, or $17.60 to $17.90 adjusted, and that it is on track to deliver another year of 10% revenue growth. Billed business was $454.0 billion in Q3 versus $421.0 billion a year earlier, up 8%. Spending volume growth running just below revenue growth is consistent with the revenue target.
items.source_name: American Express Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: AmEx Q3 credit provisions $1.0B vs. $1.3B; net write-off rate 1.8%
items.take: American Express reported Q3 consolidated provisions for credit losses of $1.0 billion versus $1.3 billion a year ago, and a net write-off rate of 1.8% versus 1.9%. Consolidated expenses were $14.5 billion, up 9%, which the release attributes mainly to higher variable customer engagement costs and the U.S. Platinum Card refresh. Lower provisions helped pretax income, which the release puts up 18%.
items.source_name: American Express Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: P&G fiscal Q1 sales rise 4% to $23.3B; diluted EPS $1.97 vs. $1.95
items.take: Procter & Gamble's July-September net sales were $23,276 million versus $22,386 million a year earlier, up 4%, with organic sales growth also 4%. Diluted EPS was $1.97 versus $1.95 and core EPS was $2.00 versus $1.99, each up 1%. Sales growth outpacing per-share earnings growth by that margin is the pattern to watch as the Thorne deal enters the numbers.
items.source_name: P&G Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: P&G lifts FY27 all-in sales growth view to 2%-4% after Thorne closes
items.take: P&G updated its fiscal 2027 all-in net sales growth range to 2% to 4%, reflecting the Thorne acquisition as of October 1, 2026, while keeping organic sales growth at 1% to 3%. Core EPS growth stays in line to 3% against fiscal 2026 core EPS of $6.89, and diluted EPS growth stays 1% to 5% against $6.62. Only the reported-sales range moved; the per-share outlook did not.
items.source_name: P&G Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Gilead to buy PepStar's oral IL-23R inhibitor HCXT-2001 for $1.275B cash
items.take: Gilead agreed to acquire PepStar Therapeutics' oral IL-23R inhibitor program, HCXT-2001, for $1.275 billion in cash payable at closing, subject to customary adjustments. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, and Gilead expects the deal to reduce GAAP and non-GAAP EPS by approximately $0.79 to $0.83. The asset is in Phase 1, so the price is being paid for a program whose safety and efficacy have not been established.
items.source_name: Gilead press release (Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Zymeworks licenses DLL3 T cell engager ZW209 to Roche; $55M upfront
items.take: Zymeworks and Roche agreed a deal for ZW209, a trispecific T cell engager targeting DLL3, with $55 million upfront, $40 million on initiation of the Phase 1b trial, and up to $718 million in further milestones. Tiered royalties run from high-single-digit to mid-teen percentages of global net sales, and Roche funds the Phase 1a trial. The deal remains subject to expiration or termination of the HSR Act waiting period.
items.source_name: Zymeworks press release (SEC Form 8-K, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: P&G paid $2.60B in dividends and $1.25B in buybacks in the September quarter
items.take: P&G's 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30 shows cash dividends paid of $2,603 million and cash paid for common stock repurchases of $1,250 million, about $3,853 million in total. Common dividends declared were $1.0885 per share. The release's fiscal 2027 plan calls for dividends above $10 billion and about $5 billion of share repurchases.
items.source_name: P&G Form 10-Q, quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026

items.headline: Verizon to report Q3 2026 results Monday, Oct. 26; webcast at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: Verizon said it will report third-quarter 2026 earnings on Monday, October 26, with a webcast beginning at 8:30 a.m. ET. The press release and financial tables will be posted to its investor relations site at 7:00 a.m. ET. It is a first large-cap telecom read after AT&T and Comcast reported this week.
items.source_name: Verizon earnings date announcement (Sept. 28, 2026)

items.headline: LKQ prelim Q3 revenue $3.32B vs. $3.50B; withdraws 2026 guidance
items.take: LKQ's preliminary, unaudited Q3 revenue was $3.32 billion versus $3.50 billion in Q3 2025, with parts and services organic revenue down 5.4%. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.47 to $0.53 versus $0.84 a year earlier, and the company withdrew its full-year 2026 guidance, last updated July 30. A range rather than a final figure, plus a guidance withdrawal, leaves full results on Oct. 29 as the first real check on the damage.
items.source_name: LKQ preliminary Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: LKQ names Abbate CEO from Dec. 15; Europe EBITDA margin 4.1%-5.1% vs. 10.0%
items.take: LKQ appointed Salvatore A. Abbate President and CEO effective Dec. 15, 2026, and Andy Hamilton left as head of LKQ Europe effective Oct. 23. Europe parts and services organic revenue fell 9.8% and segment EBITDA margin was 4.1% to 5.1% versus 10.0% in Q3 2025, which the company tied to ERP implementation disruption in Germany and volume declines in the UK and Benelux. The board has engaged Alvarez & Marsal to advise on European operations, so Europe is the operating issue to watch.
items.source_name: LKQ preliminary Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: First Hawaiian Q3 diluted EPS $0.52 vs. $0.60 in Q2; provision $20.3M
items.take: First Hawaiian reported Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $0.52 versus $0.60 in Q2 and $0.59 in Q3 2025. The provision for credit losses was $20.3 million versus $5.6 million in Q2, while net interest margin rose to 3.30% from 3.25% and CET1 was 13.50% versus 13.27% at June 30. Loans and leases fell $115.1 million to $14.5 billion, so the earnings dip came from higher provisioning rather than margin.
items.source_name: First Hawaiian Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Eni Q3 adjusted net profit EUR 2.8B; 2026 buyback raised to EUR 3.8B
items.take: Eni reported Q3 2026 proforma adjusted EBIT of EUR 6 billion, which it said doubled year over year, and adjusted net profit of EUR 2.8 billion. Net debt was EUR 6.7 billion at end-Q3, and the 2026 buyback was raised to EUR 3.8 billion from EUR 3.4 billion guided last quarter. Guidance for adjusted CFFO of EUR 16.5 billion rests on a Brent assumption of $95 a barrel, so the payout depends on that scenario.
items.source_name: Eni Q3 and nine-month 2026 results release

items.headline: Eni declares EUR 0.46 extraordinary dividend, payable Dec. 9
items.take: Eni set an extraordinary dividend of EUR 0.46 per share, about EUR 1.3 billion, payable Dec. 9, 2026 with ex-dividend date Dec. 7 and record date Dec. 8; ADRs receive EUR 0.92, payable Jan. 8, 2027. It confirmed the 2026 ordinary dividend at EUR 1.1 per share, up 5% from 2025. Q3 cash returns totaled EUR 1.9 billion, split between EUR 0.8 billion of dividend and EUR 1.1 billion of buybacks.
items.source_name: Eni Q3 and nine-month 2026 results release

items.headline: Signify Q3 sales EUR 1,367M; adjusted EBITA margin 10.6% vs. 9.7%
items.take: Signify reported Q3 2026 sales of EUR 1,367 million with comparable sales growth of -3.4% versus -3.9% in Q3 2025. Adjusted EBITA was EUR 145 million versus EUR 136 million, and the 10.6% margin included a EUR 28 million, or 2.1%, net benefit from the US tariff refund. Free cash flow was EUR 118 million versus EUR 71 million, so without the refund the margin gain would have been smaller than it looks.
items.source_name: Signify Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: First Citizens Q3 net income $606M vs. $672M in Q2; loans $157.19B
items.take: First Citizens BancShares reported Q3 2026 net income of $606 million versus $672 million in the second quarter, and net income available to common stockholders of $577 million, or $51.23 per common share. Loans and leases were $157.19 billion at Sept. 30 versus $151.03 billion at June 30, and deposits were $185.26 billion, up $11.84 billion, or 6.8%, from June 30. The release compares results with the linked quarter rather than a year ago, so the sequential decline in earnings is the cleaner read.
items.source_name: First Citizens Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: First Citizens adds buyback of up to $1.2B through 2027; CET1 10.24%
items.take: First Citizens authorized repurchases of up to $1.2 billion of its Class A common shares through 2027. At Sept. 30 its estimated CET1 ratio was 10.24%, and Q3 net charge-offs were $103 million, or 0.27% of average loans. Net interest income was $1.70 billion, up $43 million from the second quarter, so the repurchase plan sits alongside capital that the company reports above 10%.
items.source_name: First Citizens Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Rogers Q3 revenue C$5,443M vs. C$5,348M; diluted EPS C$0.88 vs. C$10.54
items.take: Rogers Communications reported Q3 2026 revenue of C$5,443 million versus C$5,348 million, adjusted EBITDA of C$2,535 million versus C$2,515 million, and diluted EPS of C$0.88 versus C$10.54. Adjusted diluted EPS was C$1.29 versus C$1.37, and the prior-year quarter included a non-cash gain from the MLSE revaluation. The company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook and declared a C$0.50 per share dividend on Oct. 22, so the headline EPS drop reflects the year-ago gain rather than operations.
items.source_name: Rogers Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: Balchem Q3 net sales $290.7M, up 8.6%; diluted EPS $1.46 vs. $1.24
items.take: Balchem reported Q3 2026 net sales of $290.7 million versus $267.6 million, an increase of 8.6%, and GAAP net earnings of $46.7 million versus $40.3 million, up 16.0%. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.46 versus $1.24, and adjusted EPS was $1.57 versus $1.35. Earnings grew faster than sales, which points to improved profitability on the revenue base.
items.source_name: Balchem Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: Flagstar Q3 provision $76M vs. $18M in Q2; CET1 12.38%
items.take: Flagstar Bank reported Q3 2026 net income attributable to common stockholders of $3 million, or $0.01 per diluted share, versus $26 million, or $0.06, in Q2 and a $45 million loss, or $0.11 per share, in Q3 2025. The provision for credit losses was $76 million versus $18 million in Q2, and net interest income was $460 million, up 8% from Q3 2025. CET1 fell to 12.38% from 13.16% at June 30, so credit costs and capital are the figures to watch.
items.source_name: Flagstar Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Kinsale Q3 diluted EPS $4.36 vs. $6.09; gross written premiums $462.9M
items.take: Kinsale Capital reported Q3 2026 net income of $98.1 million, or $4.36 per diluted share, versus $141.6 million and $6.09 a year earlier. Gross written premiums were $462.9 million, down 4.8% from $486.3 million, and the combined ratio was 75.4% versus 74.9%. Diluted operating EPS was $5.70 versus $5.21, so operating earnings rose even as GAAP net income fell.
items.source_name: Kinsale Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: Boston Beer Q3 net revenue $520.1M vs. $537.5M; diluted EPS $4.21 vs. $4.25
items.take: Boston Beer reported Q3 2026 net revenue of $520.1 million versus $537.5 million, net income of $43.2 million versus $46.2 million, and GAAP diluted EPS of $4.21 versus $4.25; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.37. Depletions were down 5% and shipments down 4.9% to about 1.8 million barrels, while gross margin rose to 51.7% from 50.8%. Revenue fell about 3.2% on lower volume, with margin improvement cushioning the hit to earnings.
items.source_name: Boston Beer Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Boston Beer lifts 2026 non-GAAP EPS floor to $9.00; range $9.00-$10.50
items.take: Boston Beer now expects 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $9.00 to $10.50, up from $8.50 to $10.50, and cut its tariff cost estimate to $18 million-$22 million from $20 million-$30 million. Year-to-date GAAP results show a net loss of $50.5 million, including litigation expense of $194.5 million, or $14.51 per share; the company held $308.1 million of cash with no debt at Sept. 26. The gap between GAAP and non-GAAP guidance is driven by that litigation charge.
items.source_name: Boston Beer Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: FirstCash Q3 revenue $1,101.2M vs. $935.6M; diluted EPS $2.33 vs. $1.86
items.take: FirstCash reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1,101.167 million versus $935.579 million, net income of $101.152 million versus $82.807 million, and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.33 versus $1.86; adjusted diluted EPS was $2.68 versus $2.26. The company said revenue and segment income from its pawn segments each increased 28%. Revenue rose about 17.7% while GAAP EPS rose about 25.3%, so earnings grew faster than sales.
items.source_name: FirstCash Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: FirstCash declares $0.46 quarterly dividend, annualized $1.84 vs. $1.68; 3,352 stores
items.take: FirstCash's board declared a $0.46 per share fourth-quarter dividend, payable Nov. 24 to holders of record Nov. 13; the annualized rate is $1.84 versus $1.68 previously, which the company describes as a 10% increase. It had 3,352 locations at Sept. 30, including 1,215 in the U.S., 1,839 in Latin America and 298 in the U.K., with 14 added in Q3. The dividend increase is modest next to the 28% pawn-segment growth the company reported.
items.source_name: FirstCash Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Waste Connections Q3 revenue $2,638.1M vs. $2,458.4M; diluted EPS $1.43 vs. $1.11
items.take: Waste Connections reported Q3 2026 revenue of $2,638.081 million versus $2,458.378 million a year earlier, net income of $359.224 million versus $286.271 million, and diluted EPS of $1.43 versus $1.11. Adjusted EPS was $1.58 versus $1.44, and adjusted EBITDA was $895.781 million, a 34.0% margin versus 33.8%. Revenue growth of about 7.3% came with a margin that barely moved, so most of the profit gain came from volume and pricing rather than from margin expansion.
items.source_name: Waste Connections Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Waste Connections raises 2026 outlook to ~$10.09B revenue; quarterly dividend $0.350
items.take: Waste Connections' updated 2026 outlook calls for revenue of approximately $10.09 billion, adjusted EBITDA of approximately $3.345 billion, and adjusted free cash flow of $1.40 billion to $1.45 billion; the release calls it the second increase this year. The quarterly dividend was $0.350 per share versus $0.315, and acquisitions closed year to date represent approximately $130 million in annualized revenues. The outlook excludes additional acquisitions, so the raise reflects the existing book of business.
items.source_name: Waste Connections Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: First Western Q3 diluted EPS $0.60 vs. $0.32; assets under management $7.21B
items.take: First Western Financial reported Q3 2026 net income available to common shareholders of $5,981 thousand versus $3,186 thousand a year earlier and diluted EPS of $0.60 versus $0.32. Assets under management were $7.21 billion, down 2.9% from Q3 2025, and loans held for investment were $2.81 billion, up 8.4%. Earnings growth came while managed assets shrank, so balance-sheet lending rather than fee-based assets drove the improvement.
items.source_name: First Western Financial Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: South Plains Financial Q3 net income $20.8M vs. $16.3M; loans $3.83B vs. $3.05B
items.take: South Plains Financial, parent of City Bank, reported Q3 2026 net income of $20,765 thousand versus $16,318 thousand and diluted EPS of $1.06 versus $0.96. Loans held for investment were $3,831 million versus $3,054 million and total deposits were $4,661 million versus $3,881 million, with total assets of $5,411 million versus $4,479 million. Loans grew about 25.5% year over year while diluted EPS rose about 10.4%, so earnings grew more slowly than the balance sheet.
items.source_name: South Plains Financial Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Bank of Japan Policy Board meets Oct. 29-30; Outlook Report due Oct. 30
items.take: The Bank of Japan's published 2026 schedule has its next Monetary Policy Meeting on October 29-30, with the quarterly Outlook Report scheduled for October 30. The remaining 2026 meeting after that is December 17-18. The October meeting is the one that carries updated forecasts, so it is the Bank's main scheduled communication before year-end.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan, Monetary Policy Meetings schedule

items.headline: Intel to report Q3 2026 results Oct. 29 after the market closes
items.take: Intel announced it will release third-quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, October 29, 2026, promptly after the market closes, with its earnings call at 2:00 p.m. PDT the same day. The date falls on the first day of the Bank of Japan's October 29-30 policy meeting. A large semiconductor report and a major central bank meeting therefore land on the same day.
items.source_name: Intel Investor Relations

items.headline: Hertz sells 50% of Oro Mobility voting units to investors for about $80.9M cash
items.take: Hertz disclosed in an 8-K (Items 1.01 and 7.01) that Cohen Private Ventures and funds affiliated with Certares and/or Knighthead bought Class A units of Oro Mobility Holdings for about $80.89 million in cash, closing October 19, 2026. The units carry 50% of the voting units and about 15.86% of the common units, and Hertz put about $60.03 million of cash plus Oro business assets into the entity first. The structure splits control evenly while Hertz keeps most of the economics.
items.source_name: Hertz Global Holdings Form 8-K (event date Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Hertz to repurchase $51.1M of 8.000% 2029 exchangeable notes for about $20.9M
items.take: In the same 8-K, Hertz agreed to repurchase about $51.1 million principal of its 8.000% Exchangeable Senior Second-Lien Secured Paid-in-Kind Notes due 2029 from certain Certares and/or Knighthead affiliates for about $20.86 million, which the filing describes as a 60% discount to par. By our calculation the price is 40.8% of principal. The filing does not state how Hertz will use proceeds from the investor purchase or the note repurchase.
items.source_name: Hertz Global Holdings Form 8-K (event date Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Hertz-Oro deal: fleet leases of about $13.7M a month, 0.5% royalty on new rental revenue
items.take: Under the Oro Mobility agreements in Hertz's 8-K, Hertz leases or subleases fleet vehicles to the new entity at about $13.7 million per month with an average term of about 4.5 years. A services agreement dated October 19 has IT, security and systems support moving to the entity within 12 months, and a 24-month royalty-bearing trademark license carries a royalty of 0.5% of new rental customer revenue. The entity's six-person board has three Hertz designees and three designated by the investors.
items.source_name: Hertz Global Holdings Form 8-K (event date Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Forge Nano Holdings lists on Nasdaq as NANO after merger with SPAC Archimedes Tech II
items.take: Forge Nano announced October 22 that, following its business combination with Archimedes Tech SPAC Partners II Co. (NASDAQ: ATII), the combined Forge Nano Holdings, Inc. common stock and warrants trade on Nasdaq as NANO and NANOW, with a ceremonial bell ringing expected October 28. The release does not disclose merger proceeds, PIPE size or valuation. It cites a $100 million U.S. Department of Energy grant for domestic battery manufacturing.
items.source_name: Forge Nano press release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: JAKKS Pacific Q3 net sales $254.2M, up 20%; diluted EPS $2.48 vs. $1.74
items.take: JAKKS Pacific reported Q3 net sales of $254.2 million versus $211.2 million a year earlier, net income of $29.9 million versus $19.9 million, and diluted EPS of $2.48 versus $1.74. Adjusted EBITDA was $44.4 million versus $36.5 million. The release gives no financial outlook, so the quarter stands as a reported result rather than a signal on holiday demand.
items.source_name: JAKKS Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Hexcel Q3 sales $496.4M, up 8.8%; adjusted EPS $0.50 vs. $0.37
items.take: Hexcel reported Q3 net sales of $496.4 million versus $456.2 million, GAAP diluted EPS of $0.50 versus $0.26, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50 versus $0.37. Commercial Aerospace sales were $330.3 million versus $274.2 million, up 20.5%. The company left 2026 guidance unchanged, so the commercial aerospace line is the driver to watch.
items.source_name: Hexcel Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Hexcel raises buyback authorization to $750.0M from $381M; no Q3 repurchases
items.take: Hexcel did not repurchase shares in Q3 2026, and about $380.6 million of authorization remained at Sept. 30. The board then raised the total authorization to $750.0 million from $381 million. 2026 guidance was left unchanged at sales of $2.025 billion to $2.125 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.30 to $2.40, so the larger authorization adds capacity rather than signalling near-term repurchases.
items.source_name: Hexcel Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Sonoco Q3 net sales $2,042M, down 4.2%; GAAP loss $7.36/share on $829M impairment
items.take: Sonoco reported Q3 net sales of $2,042 million versus $2,131 million and a GAAP diluted loss of $7.36 per share versus EPS of $1.23, including an $829 million non-cash goodwill impairment. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.67 versus $1.92. Excluding the impairment, the operating picture is a modest decline, with adjusted EBITDA of $352 million versus $386 million.
items.source_name: Sonoco Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Sonoco sets 2026 adjusted EPS at $5.30-$5.50; adds $800M term loans, draws $500M
items.take: Sonoco's revised 2026 outlook calls for net sales of $7.20 billion to $7.40 billion, adjusted EPS of $5.30 to $5.50 and adjusted EBITDA of $1.20 billion to $1.25 billion. On Sept. 25 it added $800 million in term loan facilities and drew $500 million to refinance a term loan due in 2028. The release attributes Q3 pressure to price/cost and weather-hit vegetable harvests in Consumer Packaging.
items.source_name: Sonoco Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Intuitive Q3 revenue $3.05B, up 22%; GAAP EPS $1.49 vs. $1.95; non-GAAP $3.00
items.take: Intuitive reported Q3 revenue of $3.05 billion versus $2.51 billion, GAAP diluted EPS of $1.49 versus $1.95, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $3.00 versus $2.40. GAAP EPS includes a $450 million pre-tax antitrust litigation charge. Net income attributable to Intuitive was $523 million versus $704 million, so the GAAP decline reflects the charge rather than weaker operations.
items.source_name: Intuitive Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Intuitive Q3 da Vinci placements 546 vs. 427; installed base 12,094, up 12%
items.take: Intuitive placed 546 da Vinci systems in Q3 versus 427 a year earlier, including 315 da Vinci 5 systems, and ended September with an installed base of 12,094, up 12%. Worldwide procedures grew about 15%, with da Vinci up about 14% and Ion up about 31%. Full-year da Vinci procedure growth is guided to about 14% to 15%, which the company says should land closer to the midpoint.
items.source_name: Intuitive Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: JAKKS Q3 dolls and role-play sales $119.2M, up 29%; North America up 27.5%
items.take: JAKKS reported Toys/Consumer Products sales of $192.0 million, up 23%, led by Dolls, Role-Play/Dress-Up at $119.2 million versus $92.3 million. Costumes were $62.2 million, up 12.9%, while North America sales rose 27.5% to $208.8 million and International fell 4.3% to $45.4 million. Growth was concentrated in the U.S. market, a mix that leaves results tied to North American retail demand.
items.source_name: JAKKS Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Omnicom Q3 revenue $6.42B; diluted EPS $2.38 vs. $1.75; adjusted $2.73
items.take: Omnicom reported Q3 revenue of $6,422.8 million versus $4,037.1 million a year earlier, net income attributable to Omnicom of $656.0 million versus $341.3 million, and diluted EPS of $2.38 versus $1.75. The release says the year-over-year change mostly reflects the Interpublic acquisition, which closed Nov. 26, 2025; core operations revenue was $6,010.7 million, with organic growth of 7.2%. Reported comparisons therefore overstate underlying growth, and the core figures are the cleaner read.
items.source_name: Omnicom Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: Omnicom adjusted EBITA $1,130.1M, 17.6% margin; $0.80 quarterly dividend declared
items.take: Omnicom's Q3 adjusted EBITA was $1,130.1 million at a 17.6% margin, versus $651.0 million at 16.1% a year earlier, and operating income was $991.7 million versus $530.1 million. Non-GAAP adjusted diluted EPS was $2.73 versus $2.24, and dividends declared per share were $0.80 versus $0.70. The CEO said the company is on track to deliver $900 million in cost-reduction synergies in 2026.
items.source_name: Omnicom Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: NVR Q3 net income $248.6M, diluted EPS $89.45 vs. $112.33
items.take: NVR reported Q3 net income of $248.6 million versus $342.7 million a year earlier, and diluted EPS of $89.45 versus $112.33. Consolidated revenues were $2.40 billion versus $2.61 billion, and homebuilding gross profit margin was 18.3% versus 21.0%. Revenue and margin both declined from a year earlier.
items.source_name: NVR Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: NVR Q3 new orders 4,391 units vs. 4,735; backlog 10,121 units, up 10%
items.take: NVR's Q3 new orders were 4,391 units versus 4,735 a year earlier, at an average price of $442,100 versus $464,800. Settlements were 5,268 units at an average price of $445,900. Backlog at Sept. 30 was 10,121 units, up 10% from 9,165, and $4.59 billion, up 4%, so orders fell while the order book still grew year over year.
items.source_name: NVR Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Danaher Q3 sales $6.55B, up 8.5%; diluted EPS $1.75 vs. $1.27
items.take: Danaher reported Q3 sales of $6,554 million versus $6,053 million a year earlier, up 8.5%, with core sales growth of 3.0% (5.5% excluding respiratory testing). Net earnings were $1,235 million versus $908 million, and diluted EPS was $1.75 versus $1.27. Adjusted diluted EPS from continuing operations was $2.11 versus $1.89.
items.source_name: Danaher Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Danaher raises 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $8.57-$8.62; Q3 free cash flow $1.63B
items.take: Danaher raised its full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance for continuing operations to $8.57-$8.62 from $8.45-$8.60 and guides to core sales growth of approximately 2.5%. Q3 operating cash flow from continuing operations was $1,886 million versus $1,662 million, and free cash flow was $1,632 million versus $1,370 million. Cash generation grew faster than reported sales in the quarter.
items.source_name: Danaher Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Verisign Q3 revenue $443.0M vs. $419.1M; diluted EPS $2.35 vs. $2.27
items.take: Verisign reported Q3 revenue of $443.0 million versus $419.1 million a year earlier, operating income of $296.5 million versus $284.3 million, and net income of $212.6 million versus $212.8 million. Diluted EPS was $2.35 versus $2.27. Net income was essentially flat while diluted EPS rose, which implies a smaller diluted share count.
items.source_name: Verisign Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Verisign .com/.net base 182.5M, up 6.1%; $189M buyback in Q3
items.take: Verisign said the .com and .net domain name base was 182.5 million registrations at Sept. 30, 2026, up 6.1% year over year, with a net increase of 3.36 million in Q3. It repurchased 0.7 million shares for $189 million in the quarter and had $1.36 billion remaining under its authorization at quarter-end.
items.source_name: Verisign Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Enova Q3 revenue $1.01B, up 26%; diluted EPS $4.06 vs. $3.03
items.take: Enova International reported Q3 total revenue of $1,009.2 million versus $802.7 million a year earlier, and net income of $107.3 million versus $80.3 million. Diluted EPS was $4.06 versus $3.03; adjusted EPS was $4.48 versus $3.36. Revenue growth outpaced earnings-per-share growth only modestly, with net revenue margin rising to 61% from 57%.
items.source_name: Enova Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: TGS Q3 revenue $397M vs. $388M; order backlog $679M, up 52%
items.take: TGS reported Q3 revenue of USD 397 million versus USD 388 million a year earlier, and EBIT of USD 86 million versus USD 94 million, including a USD 41 million gain from the sale of its well data business. Order backlog was USD 679 million, up 52% year over year, and Q3 order inflow was USD 357 million. The company said contract revenues were its highest since Q4 2024.
items.source_name: TGS Q3 2026 results release

items.headline: Enova combined loan receivables up 30% to a record $5.9B; charge-offs 8.1%
items.take: Enova said period-end combined loan and finance receivables rose 30% from a year earlier to a record $5.9 billion, with the consolidated net charge-off ratio at 8.1% versus 8.5% in Q3 2025. It repurchased $46 million of common stock in the quarter. Faster balance growth alongside a lower reported charge-off ratio is the combination the company is pointing to.
items.source_name: Enova Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: TGS trims 2026 multi-client investment guide to ~$510M from ~$550M
items.take: TGS said it now expects 2026 multi-client investments of approximately USD 510 million, compared with prior guidance of approximately USD 550 million, and declared a dividend of USD 0.155 per share payable in Q4 2026.
